business_question: What does a typical selected meal weigh at the lunch line?
definition: The median of derived_selected_meal_weight_g over the core-ready registered-export sessions.
does_not_tell_us: How much food was actually consumed, left over or wasted; it says nothing about intake.
exclusions: the two quarantined crossover sessions (they are not core-ready); the non-registered-export population; exact-duplicate rows (left out of the sums that build the weight)
filters: population D only; no filter beyond the population; WARN and INFO findings, weather and volume flags never filter a metric
interpretation: Typical DERIVED selected meal weight in the approved measurement population.
limitation: DERIVED from weighing events at the line; one population; five weeks; cannot be read as intake.
lineage: metric -> fact_dining_session rows (population filter) -> session_key -> fact_weighing_event rows (event_id = source_file#row) -> stg_weighing_event -> raw source file and row
null_handling: a NULL weight is excluded and counted; it is never read as 0; an empty population raises
population_rationale: The approved measurement population: registered-export sessions that meet the core readiness criteria. Never pooled with the other export.
quarantine_handling: quarantined sessions have no canonical weight and are outside population D; they contribute nothing and remain listed
statistical_method: median: middle value of the sorted weights (mean of the two middle values for an even count)
tells_us: The typical weight a session recorded across its selected components at the lunch line.

business_question: How heavy is a large selection: the weight that 90% of sessions do not exceed?
definition: The 90th percentile of derived_selected_meal_weight_g over the core-ready registered-export sessions, by linear interpolation.
does_not_tell_us: How much food was actually consumed, left over or wasted; it says nothing about intake.
interpretation: Upper end of the DERIVED selected meal weight distribution.
limitation: the most period-sensitive metric; describes five weeks; DERIVED, not intake.
lineage: metric -> fact_dining_session rows (population filter) -> session_key -> fact_weighing_event rows (event_id = source_file#row) -> stg_weighing_event -> raw source file and row
statistical_method: linear interpolation at position (n - 1) * 0.90 of the sorted weights; identical to numpy/pandas quantile(0.9) and R type 7; not nearest-rank
tells_us: How heavy the heavier selections are (the 90th percentile).

business_question: How many registered-export sessions meet the core readiness criteria and therefore contribute to the KPIs?
definition: The number of registered-export session keys that satisfy the core readiness contract: not quarantined, at least one modellable event, no ERROR finding, valid weights, parsed times.
does_not_tell_us: Demand, customers, diners, visits, transactions or traffic; it does not measure how busy the restaurant was.
exclusions: the two quarantined crossover sessions (kept in M5's denominator); the non-registered-export population
filters: population D only; no filter beyond the population; WARN and INFO findings, weather and volume flags never filter a metric
grain: one session key (session_id|registered_export); per service date in the supporting table
interpretation: How many registered-export sessions were observed, are valid and feed M1, M2 and M4.
limitation: an observation of the export; the weekday pattern and six irregular days mean it must not be read as restaurant volume.
lineage: metric -> fact_dining_session rows (population filter) -> session_key -> fact_weighing_event rows (event_id = source_file#row) -> stg_weighing_event -> raw source file and row
population_rationale: The same approved measurement population as M1, M2 and M4.
quarantine_handling: quarantined sessions are outside population D and listed in the quarantine manifest
tells_us: How many valid registered-export sessions the export contains.

business_question: How broad is a typical selection, counted in distinct normalized component names?
definition: The median of distinct_component_count over the core-ready registered-export sessions, where a component is a distinct name after trim, whitespace collapse and case-fold.
does_not_tell_us: Which dishes were chosen, nutritional variety, or how much of anything was eaten.
interpretation: How many different named components a typical session selected.
limitation: counts names within a session; no alias table, so different spellings of one dish would count separately; comparison of components across exports is limited on some days.
lineage: metric -> fact_dining_session rows (population filter) -> session_key -> fact_weighing_event rows (event_id = source_file#row) -> stg_weighing_event -> raw source file and row
metric_name: Median Distinct Normalized Components per Session
null_handling: a NULL count is excluded and counted; never read as 0
statistical_method: median: middle value of the sorted counts
tells_us: How many distinct component names a typical session recorded.

business_question: What share of the eligible registered-export sessions can be reconstructed and used?
definition: Core-ready registered-export sessions divided by all eligible registered-export sessions, the denominator being fixed before any quarantine or removal.
does_not_tell_us: That the data, the meals or the measurements are correct or accurate, or that sessions are free of warnings.
exclusions: none from the denominator; the two quarantined crossover sessions are simply not core-ready
filters: numerator population D; denominator population C
interpretation: Share of eligible registered-export sessions meeting the approved core measurement readiness criteria.
limitation: high because few registered-export sessions carry an ERROR finding, not because the data is proven error-free; weather, WARN rules and volume flags never enter it.
lineage: metric -> fact_dining_session rows (population filter) -> session_key -> fact_weighing_event rows (event_id = source_file#row) -> stg_weighing_event -> raw source file and row
population_rationale: The denominator is every registered-export session in the source (1,699), counted before removal, so the quarantined sessions stay visible in it. It is never recomputed after removal.
quarantine_handling: quarantined sessions stay in the denominator and are absent from the numerator; that explains the 2-session gap
tells_us: What share of the eligible registered-export sessions meet the core readiness criteria.

business_question: For what share of eligible registered-export sessions is a weather observation joined?
definition: Eligible registered-export sessions with weather_matched, divided by all eligible registered-export sessions.
does_not_tell_us: That weather affected weight, dining behaviour or anything else.
exclusions: none; the two quarantined sessions are NOT_ATTEMPTED (the model does not join quarantined sessions), so they are unmatched here
interpretation: Coverage of the contextual weather join (next full UTC hour after the first weighing; r_1h is the hour ending at its timestamp).
limitation: context only; regional station roughly 6 km away; the profiling dry run matched all 1,697 core-ready sessions and expected the two quarantined sessions to be joined too, which the model deliberately does not do.
lineage: metric -> fact_dining_session rows (population filter) -> session_key -> fact_weighing_event rows (event_id = source_file#row) -> stg_weighing_event -> raw source file and row; weather join -> fact_weather (station x UTC hour) -> stg_weather_observation
null_handling: NULL weather values are counted separately and never filled
numerator: eligible registered-export sessions with a joined weather observation
quarantine_handling: quarantined sessions are not joined and count as unmatched
tells_us: Whether a weather observation is available for the session's hour.

business_question: What share of eligible registered-export sessions carry no session-level warning?
definition: Core-ready registered-export sessions with no session-level WARN (B04, B07, T04, T05, I06), divided by all eligible registered-export sessions.
does_not_tell_us: Whether the data is correct, or that flagged sessions are wrong (a WARN is a diagnostic flag).
exclusions: event-level warnings (B02, I02), file-level (T07) and day-level (C02) flags are not counted
interpretation: Share of eligible registered-export sessions with no session-level warning.
limitation: a diagnostic of how many sessions carry a WARN, not a data-quality score; it differs from M5 because a WARN never removes a session from the KPIs.
lineage: metric -> fact_dining_session rows (population filter) -> session_key -> fact_weighing_event rows (event_id = source_file#row) -> stg_weighing_event -> raw source file and row
numerator: core-ready registered-export sessions with no session-level WARN
quarantine_handling: quarantined sessions stay in the denominator and are not in the numerator
tells_us: How many eligible sessions carry no session-level warning.

business_question: How does the warn-free rate change if event-level warnings are also counted?
definition: As S2, but a session with an event-level WARN (B02, I02) and no session-level WARN also counts as warned.
does_not_tell_us: A better or truer warn-free figure; S2 is the approved one.
exclusions: as S2 plus event-level warnings are counted
formula: 100 * COUNT(core_ready AND NOT has_session_warn AND NOT has_event_warn) / COUNT(C)
interpretation: Reconciliation of S2 to the event-level view (three sessions differ). It never replaces S2.
limitation: diagnostic only; reported so the S2 definition is transparent.
lineage: metric -> fact_dining_session rows (population filter) -> session_key -> fact_weighing_event rows (event_id = source_file#row) -> stg_weighing_event -> raw source file and row
metric_name: Warn-Free Rate incl. Event-Level Warnings (diagnostic variant)
numerator: core-ready sessions with no session-level or event-level WARN
tells_us: How much the choice of which WARN rules count changes the rate.

definition: BLOCKED / SOURCE GAP. The Flavoria system documents lunch-line waste measurement keyed on tray, but no direct waste records are available in the public data this project can reach.
does_not_tell_us: Any amount of food waste, consumption, or leftovers, or any ratio to selected weight.
formula: none: there is no formula, no estimate and no proxy
interpretation: No direct waste metric is computed. derived_selected_meal_weight_g is not waste and is not used as a proxy.
limitation: permanent unless a public raw waste dataset is found.
tells_us: That direct waste data exists conceptually and is not publicly available here.
